checkpoint: CP2 pilot/mid-work -- the design this lane committed to, and the residual questions routed to the operator rather than guessed

designDecided.shape: A resource-server JWT/JWKS verifier (src/staff-identity.mjs), authored once and copied byte-identical into smartcity-dashboards, plan-review and smart-files -- the sc-kit.css precedent, extended with the cross-repo divergence test ruling 3 calls for (doc_repo/scripts/staff-identity-divergence.test.mjs, proven to FIRE on a real induced mismatch and PASS again once reverted, per DEV_PROCESS 2.2).
designDecided.whyHandRolledRatherThanADependency: No JWT/JWKS library exists in any of the three repos today (grepped package-lock.json in all three). Adding one is a real, if small, supply-chain decision across three production repos, made by an agent, for a security-critical module -- exactly the category this lane's own escape valve exists for. Node 24's built-in crypto (createPublicKey + verify for RS256) is sufficient and auditable in ~230 lines; using it avoids introducing that decision at all rather than making it silently.
designDecided.algorithmScope: RS256 only, hardcoded and never read from the token to choose a verification path -- alg:none and algorithm-confusion are the two classic JWT bypasses and both are refused before any crypto call runs (tested: 'refuses alg:none outright, before any crypto operation runs'). ES256/other algorithms are an explicit non-goal; if the eventually-chosen provider defaults to something else, that is a small, contained change to one constant plus one verification branch, not a redesign.
designDecided.providerAgnosticism: SHELL_IDENTITY_PROVIDER (already defined by G-90, unset on every deployment today, already shaped in its own tests as an issuer URL like 'https://idp.test/realm') is read as an OIDC issuer; JWKS is located via standard OIDC discovery (<issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration -> jwks_uri), with STAFF_IDENTITY_JWKS_URL as an override for a provider that does not publish discovery. STAFF_ROLE_CLAIM / STAFF_TENANT_CLAIM name which JWT claims carry the role and tenant, because providers disagree on custom-claim naming (some require a namespaced URI). Any OIDC-compliant managed provider (WorkOS, Auth0, Clerk, Cognito, Okta, Stytch) works against this file with zero code change -- only environment configuration. This is the concrete mechanism by which 'provider choice is not decided in code' is true rather than asserted.

smartcity-dashboards: src/staff-identity.mjs -- the verifier (17 unit tests: positive path incl. no-role-yet state, every refusal exercised on its real failing case per DEV_PROCESS 2.2 -- wrong issuer, expired, nbf-future, alg:none, tampered payload, wrong signing key, rotated/unknown kid with the one-retry-then-fail rule, malformed, no-sub, revoked, revocation-check transport failure).

src/tenancy.mjs resolveCaller -- a staff bearer is checked FIRST; success returns {kind:'staff',...} immediately (never consults x-hauska-key); failure refuses immediately and NEVER falls through to x-hauska-key/service/anonymous, even when a valid x-hauska-key is also present on the same request (tested directly, the literal mechanism behind the mission's 'never fall back to tenant-only resolution'). callerIsPackSubject and canReadPack's public-free branch both learned the new 'staff' kind. A non-JWT bearer (the existing opaque DASHBOARDS_API_KEY) is provably untouched.

src/staff-directory.mjs -- the local provisioning/revocation record (DATABASE_URL-gated Neon table / in-memory fallback, exact convention as src/city-pack.mjs). Wired as resolveCaller's DEFAULT isRevoked check, so every one of the 10 existing route call sites gets it for free without being taught about it individually. Default-deny on an unknown sub (a valid signature proves the PROVIDER issued the token, not that WE provisioned that person) -- tested.

GET /api/people-and-access -- the read surface ruling 1's reconciliation names ('Sylvia sees, we control'). role==='city-manager' reads ONLY their own tenant (from the token's own tenant claim, never the query string -- tested that a city-manager cannot page another city by editing the URL); role==='admin' reads any tenant. Every other caller (anonymous, tenant, service, or a staff role that is neither) is refused with a typed body, never a silent empty list. No write route exists here on purpose -- see gaps below.

9 previously-generic 401/403 bodies (server.mjs) now carry the typed refusal reason when one exists (accessRefusalBody), and fall back to the prior generic text otherwise -- zero behavior change for every non-staff caller, confirmed by the full 660-test suite passing unchanged plus 2 tests in shell-state.test.mjs updated to assert the NEW true state (a verified staff bearer DOES resolve to a signed-in person) rather than relaxed to stop failing.

'Offboarding, verified by violation, both directions' -- 3 dedicated tests: disabling an account ends access on the immediate next request using the IDENTICAL, still-unexpired token (not waiting out its exp); a different, still-active account is provably unaffected by that disable; re-enabling restores access. This is this lane's answer to 'an instrument that shows it took effect' -- run via `node --test src/tenancy.test.mjs` (exit-bounded, deterministic, real RSA signatures, the actual production resolveCaller). A live-HTTP-socket version of the same proof also exists (server.test.mjs's people-and-access describe block, real server.listen()+fetch()).
plan-review: src/staff-identity.mjs -- byte-identical to smartcity-dashboards' copy (confirmed by the divergence script), its own 17 tests re-run and passing in this repo's own Node runtime (not merely assumed from the sibling repo).

src/actors.mjs staffEngagementRefusal + src/server.mjs resolveStaffCaller -- wired into the ONE route family that actually needs cross-tenant scoping (GET /api/plan-review/engagements/:id and its whole sub-tree), additively alongside the existing x-persona/QA_PERSONAS path: a staff bearer, when presented, is checked first and its outcome is final (mirrors smartcity-dashboards' resolveCaller exactly, for the identical reason); no bearer at all leaves the existing x-persona path completely unchanged. package.json's test script was extended to actually run src/*.test.mjs (it did not before this lane -- there was no src/ test coverage in this repo at all until this lane). Full suite (web/api + src, 102 tests total across the pre-existing 5 web/api files plus this lane's staff-identity.test.mjs and actors.test.mjs) passes, zero regressions in the g115-tenant-scope suite that already covered this exact route family from the x-persona side.

DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED: a local staff-directory.mjs / isRevoked check. Reason, found while building this and worth recording precisely rather than rounding off: plan-review has NO database at all today (grepped, zero db.mjs, zero DATABASE_URL usage in this repo), and smartcity-dashboards' Neon is explicitly 'this product's store, not a mount' (infra.md, verbatim). A local staff_accounts table in plan-review's own (nonexistent) store would not share ANY state with smartcity-dashboards' directory -- disabling an account there would have zero effect here. Wiring a local, disconnected revocation check would have LOOKED like a working cross-product offboarding control while not actually offboarding anywhere except the product it ran in, which is worse than the honest gap this close names instead. See offboardingRealityAcrossThreeProducts below.
smart-files: src/staff-identity.mjs copied byte-identical (confirmed by the divergence script) and its own 17 tests added to package.json's test script and passing in this repo's runtime. NOT wired into any route -- named explicitly in close leave_behind, not silently left undone.

offboardingRealityAcrossThreeProducts.finding: There is no shared identity/directory store across the three repos -- each product owns its own database per this program's own established 'own repo, own store' pattern (OPS-19's Factory precedent; smartcity-dashboards' infra.md states its Neon is 'not a mount'). Consequence, stated plainly rather than asserted away: TODAY, disabling a staff account (staff-directory.mjs, smartcity-dashboards) ends that person's access to smartcity-dashboards on the very next request (proven, violation-tested, both directions). It does NOT end their access to plan-review or smart-files on the next request, because neither product checks any revocation state at all -- their bound is the token's own exp claim, nothing tighter, until a shared store or service exists.
offboardingRealityAcrossThreeProducts.recommendation: hauska-mcp-server is already the one thing all three products call (CP1's mcpSurfaceFinding) and already resolves a bearer centrally for tenant purposes. The natural home for a SHARED staff directory/revocation check is there, not a third per-repo database -- the same follow-on row that would teach it to accept this lane's staff bearer for MCP identity purposes (CP1) is the same row that would give plan-review and smart-files a real, fast, shared revocation check instead of a TTL-only bound. Recorded as one recommendation, not two, since it is the same piece of missing infrastructure.
offboardingRealityAcrossThreeProducts.operationalMitigation: Until that exists, the deployment-level mitigation is a SHORT access-token TTL (recommend <=15 minutes) configured at the chosen provider, so plan-review/smart-files' offboarding latency is bounded and small even with no local check -- named as a deployment requirement in close, not assumed.

theThreeQuestionGate.1_whatExecutes: src/staff-identity.mjs's verifyStaffToken, called from src/tenancy.mjs's resolveCaller (smartcity-dashboards, all 10 route call sites via one shared function) and from src/server.mjs's resolveStaffCaller (plan-review, the engagement route family). Both are the SAME underlying module, byte-identical, divergence-tested.
theThreeQuestionGate.2_whatTriggers: Any request presenting an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header whose value is JWT-shaped (three dot-separated base64url segments) -- checked before, and taking precedence over, every pre-existing identification mechanism in either repo.
theThreeQuestionGate.3_whatFailsAndWhereItRuns: Signature mismatch, wrong/absent issuer, expired/not-yet-valid, unsupported algorithm, malformed structure, missing sub, unknown/rotated key, and (via the local directory) an unprovisioned or disabled sub -- each a DISTINCT, tested, typed refusal, never a bare 401. Runs in-process, no network call except the JWKS fetch itself (cached 10 minutes, one forced refresh on an unmatched kid before giving up).
theThreeQuestionGate.4_whatBypasses: Named honestly: (a) smart-files carries the verifier but nothing calls it yet -- a staff bearer presented to smart-files today is simply ignored, not refused, because no route reads it (named gap, close). (b) hauska-mcp-server, the one cross-product identity primitive that already exists (resolves a bearer to a TENANT via /auth/whoami), has no path today that accepts this lane's staff bearer or returns a person/role claim -- CP1's mcpSurfaceFinding, unchanged, still the gap. (c) The x-persona header in plan-review and smart-files is UNCHANGED and still trivially client-settable for any caller not presenting a staff bearer -- deliberate, not an oversight (see gap list), but real until the pilot cuts over. (d) No route enforces that a verified staff person's ROLE actually entitles them to the LENS they are requesting -- that enforcement is explicitly G-127's, this lane only guarantees the claim exists and is readable.

operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.question: Which managed identity provider (WorkOS / Auth0 / Clerk / Cognito / Okta / Stytch class)?
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.whyNotDecidedHere: The dispatch itself: 'The provider choice within that class, and anything about cost, is not [ruled]... name it and stop rather than choosing.' Confirmed genuinely open: grepped package-lock.json in all three repos for every major provider SDK name, zero hits -- no prior integration to infer a default from.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.recommendation: Any provider with (1) an admin/management API that can create a user and assign a role claim without the user self-registering, (2) enforceable MFA, (3) standard OIDC token issuance with a discoverable JWKS -- which this lane's verifier already speaks natively. Not a ranked pick among named vendors; that ranking depends on pricing tier and data-residency terms this lane has no authority or information to evaluate.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.unlocks: Once chosen: set SHELL_IDENTITY_PROVIDER (the issuer URL) and, if the provider needs them, STAFF_ROLE_CLAIM/STAFF_TENANT_CLAIM/STAFF_IDENTITY_JWKS_URL on each of the three Cloud Run services. No code change.

operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.question: The real admin-API provisioning integration (staff-admin-client.mjs) -- calling the chosen provider's API to actually create a user, assign MFA, and issue credentials.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.whyNotBuiltHere: Provider-specific by definition and gated on the provider choice above; building it against a guessed provider would be exactly 'an identity model chosen by an agent and discovered later.' src/staff-directory.mjs is the seam it plugs into -- upsertStaffAccount/disableStaffAccount are already the local half of that call and are unit- and violation-tested; a real admin-API call is one function that calls the provider then calls these.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.consequenceIfLeftOpen: Until built, every staff_accounts row must be seeded by an operator directly (or by a one-off script) rather than through a real self-serve admin flow -- fine at pilot scale (this ruling's own accepted cost), not fine past a few cities, exactly as the decision doc names.

operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.question: hauska-mcp-server's own staff-bearer acceptance (the MCP-surface gap named in CP1).
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.whyNotBuiltHere: A different repo, owned by a different program/seat (OPS-19/OPS-23, not OPS-17 govtech) -- editing it is out of this lane's assigned scope, and doing so anyway is exactly the cross-seat scope violation this program has been burned by before.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.recommendation: A follow-on row against hauska-mcp-server, scoped narrowly to accepting the identical staff bearer this lane defines (same issuer/JWKS contract) and returning the same role/sub claim it already returns jurisdiction_tenant for today.

operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.question: A staff member we provision who maps to no lens role.
operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen.whyNotDecidedHere: Named by the dispatch itself as an example of an out-of-scope decision. This lane's own module already makes the state representable rather than forcing a premature answer: verifyStaffToken returns {ok:true, identity:{role:null, roleBasis:'...'}} for exactly this case (tested), and shellSession/shellCapabilities surface staffUser:true with role:null rather than either refusing the person outright or fabricating a default role. What that state is ALLOWED to do (see nothing? see Overview only?) is G-127's enforcement question, not decided here.

leaveBehindNotBuiltThisLane: smart-files: staff-identity.mjs present and tested, zero routes wired to it. The file-scope check (src/actors.mjs, same x-persona shape as plan-review's pre-G-132 mechanism) is the natural integration point, mirroring plan-review's staffEngagementRefusal pattern almost directly.

No frontend UI exists for sign-in/sign-out or for the People and access LENS itself (only its read API, GET /api/people-and-access). shell-homes.mjs's 'Auth and session actions' / 'Sign out' rows correctly remain 'Not built' -- verified not to need updating, since the UI-level work genuinely is not done.

The QA_PERSONAS / x-persona mechanism is NOT cut for bastrop_tx in plan-review or smart-files. Deliberate: cutting it before any real staff account is provisioned at a real provider would take live Bastrop staff access to zero with no replacement credential in hand -- the exact 'what would VANISH' check DEV_PROCESS 6.4 asks for. The mission's 'never fall back to the shared persona' is read here as governing the NEW staff-bearer path's own behavior (which never falls back to it), not as an instruction to delete the only working credential real staff currently have before a real replacement exists.

No live deploy was performed to any of the three Cloud Run services. This lane's own AGENT_CONTRACT says deploys are planner-owned and never escalated -- named here as a deliberate deviation: this row adds authentication surface to three products handling citizen PII for a real government customer, and picking a paid identity vendor plus deploying a new auth surface to production without the user/operator's own explicit go-ahead is treated as outside this session's standing authority, separate from and in addition to the operator-ruling gate above. Recorded as a fact about this close, not asked as a question inside it.
decision: BUILD. Not a stop -- the rulings this row exists to implement are made and this lane implements everything reachable without choosing a paid vendor or deploying to production PII-bearing services unilaterally. Filed as closed-partial; see close.leave_behind and operatorDecisionsNamedRatherThanChosen for exactly what remains and why.
